messages:
Mira Patel: Heads up — the new "sub-slice" econ card on the cost dashboard is showing some per-invocation costs that look... off. https://redwood.app/console/costs/slices :eyes:
Jon Chen: I saw that too. Looks like a bunch of tiny slices (n=3-10) blow up the per-invocation number when one invocation hits a big model.
Samir Gomez: Yep small sample + prefetch credit attribution = noisy.
Mira Patel: Example: tenant A had 4 sampled invocations, one of them used the 13B chain and the avg jumped to $0.23/invocation which is misleading for product owners.
Laura B: Can we avoid showing raw per-invocation when sample_count < 50? Or show a warning/CI?
Jon Chen: Agreed on CI. Maybe display: avg_cost ± margin (95%CI) and a small sample badge.
Samir Gomez: Also prefetch credits are applied at batch time, not invocation time, so the per-invocation split depends on how we amortize. Right now the UI is using simple equal-split which exaggerates for tiny slices.
Mira Patel: Proposed options: 1) hide per-invocation for sample_count < X, 2) show smoothed estimate (bayesian prior), 3) show amortized cost with a tooltip explaining prefetch. Which do we prefer?
Jon Chen: Lean 2 + 3. Smoothing with a prior anchored to route-level mean will avoid big jumps. Then let power users opt out to see raw.
Laura B: UX: if we do smoothing we need a clear affordance: a toggle labeled "show sampled/raw" and a tooltip "smoothed to reduce small-sample variance". Also show sample_count and total_tokens_sampled inline.
Samir Gomez: Implementation notes: backend currently returns fields: total_token_cost, sample_count, raw_per_invocation. We can add 'smoothed_per_invocation' and 'ci_lower','ci_upper'. SQL-ish prototype I used:```sql
-- weighted bayes-like smoothing
SELECT
 route,
 (sum(cost) + prior_mean * prior_weight) / (count(*) + prior_weight) AS smoothed_cost,
 percentile_cont(0.025) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY cost) AS ci_lower,
 percentile_cont(0.975) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY cost) AS ci_upper
FROM sampled_invocations
WHERE window = '7d'
GROUP BY route;
```
Mira Patel: Nice. What prior_weight are you using?
Samir Gomez: Started with 20 invocations / route and prior_mean = global route avg. We can tune.
Jon Chen: Two other edgecases: 1) prefetched tokens credited to a different route (prefetch pipeline) and 2) canary traffic where route-level mean is changing quickly.
Laura B: For canaries we should show a 'volatile' badge when the route's variance in last 24h > threshold. That way PMs don't overreact.
Mira Patel: Agree. Also we need to make sure the console explains that caching savings are sometimes credited upstream — that explains sudden negative per-invocation numbers.
Jon Chen: On the API side, we should add fields to /costs/v1/route_summary: sample_count, total_tokens_sampled, amortized_prefetch_credit, smoothed_per_invocation, ci_lower, ci_upper, volatility_flag. Backwards-compatible: keep raw fields too.
Samir Gomez: I'll put up a quick PR for the query + aggregated fields. @Jon Chen can you expose the new fields in the API and wire the console?
Jon Chen: Yep, will schedule a small API change. Will add a feature flag: "smoothed_subslice_costs" so we can rollout gradually.
Laura B: UX checklist: badge for sample_count (tooltip explaining threshold), toggle for raw/smoothed, volatility badge, link to doc explaining amortization and prefetch. I can mock the toggle screen.
Mira Patel: Awesome. Can we get a small experiment? Phase 1: API + backend compute (internal flag). Phase 2: Console behind flag with sample_count badge. Phase 3: Default on with docs.
Samir Gomez: Timeline: PR today for aggregation, API change early next week, console mock by Laura by mid-week, deploy behind flag by end of week.
OpsBot: deploy-bot: New feature-flag created: smoothed_subslice_costs (env: staging)
Jon Chen: I'll post the API schema in #eng-platform once PR is up.
Mira Patel: Thanks all. One last ask — include a small "confidence" sparkline on hover that shows sample count trend so owners can see if it's stabilizing.
Laura B: Will add to mock.
Samir Gomez: I'll add tests for edgecases: zero-sample routes, negative amortized credits, high-variance routes.
Mira Patel: Great. If no objections I'll merge the PR tomorrow. :thumbsup:
